mainTopic: Why אחשורוש refused המן's money, the king's ring and תשובה, why there is no הלל on פורים, and the seven נביאות
overview: This amud keeps explaining the פסוקים of מגילת אסתר. It starts with a משל of a mound and a ditch, which shows that אחשורוש wanted to destroy the Jews just as much as המן did. Next, רבי אבא בר כהנא teaches that the king's ring sealing the decree brought the Jews to תשובה, something 48 נביאים and 7 נביאות could not do. A ברייתא then says those prophets added nothing to the תורה except reading the מגילה, which they learned through a קל וחומר from the שירה sung at יציאת מצרים. The גמרא asks why we don't say הלל on פורים and gives three answers: the miracle happened outside ארץ ישראל, the מגילה reading is itself the הלל (רב נחמן), and we were still servants of אחשורוש (רבא). It then explains that there were really many more prophets, but only the prophecies needed for later generations were written down. Finally, the גמרא names the seven נביאות and brings a source for each one in turn: שרה, מרים, דבורה, חנה, and אביגיל. The story of אביגיל's clever halachic exchange with דוד continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The parable: one man has a mound, the other has a ditch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a משל to explain אחשורוש and המן: two men, one with an unwanted mound and one with an unwanted ditch, each wishing he could buy what the other has.
steps.simpleTranslation: A parable for אחשורוש and המן: what is this like? Two people. One had a mound of dirt in his field, and the other had a ditch in his field. The ditch owner said, 'I wish I could buy that mound!' The mound owner said, 'I wish I could buy that ditch!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is telling a short story (a משל) to explain how אחשורוש and המן dealt with each other. This step only sets up the two characters; the punch line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man has a problem the other man can solve. The ditch owner needs dirt to fill his hole, and the mound owner needs a hole to get rid of his dirt. Each one assumes he will have to pay for the solution.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable; a story used to explain an idea
A mound or heap of dirt
If only; who would give me

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the mound owner is the 'rich' one with something valuable. Both men see their own feature as a problem, and each wants what the other has.

phrases.english: A parable of Ahasuerus and Haman:
phrases.notes: This looks back at the earlier פסוק where the king tells המן to keep the silver. The story explains why he turned the money down.

phrases.english: To what is the matter comparable?
To two people,

phrases.aramaic: לְאֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ תֵּל בְּתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ
phrases.english: one had a mound in the middle of his field

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאֶחָד הָיָה לוֹ חָרִיץ בְּתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ.
phrases.english: and the other had a ditch in the middle of his field.
The owner of the ditch said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי יִתֵּן לִי תֵּל זֶה בְּדָמִים!
phrases.english: If only someone would give me this mound, even for money!
The owner of the mound said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי יִתֵּן לִי חָרִיץ זֶה בְּדָמִים!
phrases.english: If only someone would give me this ditch, even for money!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל דַּאֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ וְהָמָן לָמָּה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage; explains the earlier פסוק in which אחשורוש refused המן's money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחשורוש and המן are like two men who each need what the other has and each think they will have to pay for it.

steps.title: The punch line: 'Take it for free, and gladly!'
steps.stepSummary: The two men meet; the ditch owner offers to buy the mound, and the mound owner tells him to take it for free. So too, אחשורוש was happy to give המן the Jews without payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some time later they met. The ditch owner said to the mound owner, 'Sell me your mound!' He answered, 'Take it for free, and I only wish you had done it sooner!'
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its point: the mound owner is so glad to get rid of his dirt that he refuses payment. This explains why אחשורוש told המן to keep his money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן offered money to destroy the Jews, as if he were buying something from the king. But אחשורוש wanted the Jews gone just as much, so he was happy to hand them over for free. The משל teaches that אחשורוש was not an innocent bystander; he shared המן's hatred.

keyTerms.meaning: And if only! (I wish it were so)

steps.whatToRemember: The משל of the mound and the ditch shows that אחשורוש wanted to destroy the Jews just as much as המן did, which is why he refused המן's money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shapes how the גמרא views אחשורוש throughout the story: a full partner in the decree, not just a king who was tricked.

phrases.english: Some time later, they met one another.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ בַּעַל חָרִיץ לְבַעַל הַתֵּל:
phrases.english: The owner of the ditch said to the owner of the mound:
Sell me your mound!

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: טוֹל אוֹתוֹ בְּחִנָּם, וְהַלְוַאי!
phrases.english: He said to him: Take it for free, and if only you would!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משל begun in step 1 and gives its point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the two men met, the mound owner gave his mound away for free. So too, אחשורוש gladly handed the Jews to המן without payment.

steps.title: The king's ring did more than all the prophets
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא teaches that אחשורוש removing his ring to seal המן's decree brought the Jews to תשובה, something 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses could not do.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the king removed his ring.' רבי אבא בר כהנא said: The removal of the ring was greater than the 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses who prophesied to Israel. They all could not bring the people back to the right path, but the removal of the ring did bring them back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק in the מגילה, about the king giving away his signet ring, and רבי אבא בר כהנא makes a striking point about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prophets spoke to the people for generations, yet the people did not fully change. Once the king sealed the decree with his ring and the danger became real, the Jews did תשובה. Fear of a real threat achieved what words of rebuke did not.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought them back to the good path; brought them to תשובה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אבא בר כהנא is not saying the ring was holier than the prophets. He means it was more effective at getting the Jews to do תשובה.

phrases.english: "And the king removed his ring"
phrases.notes: This is from אסתר chapter 3. The king gave המן his signet ring so he could seal the decree against the Jews.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said:
The removal of the ring was greater

phrases.aramaic: יוֹתֵר מֵאַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה נְבִיאִים וְשֶׁבַע נְבִיאוֹת
phrases.english: than the forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses
who prophesied to Israel,
for all of them did not bring them back to the right way,
whereas the removal of the ring brought them back to the right way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיָּסַר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶת טַבַּעְתּוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the מגילה after finishing the משל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sealing of the decree with the king's ring brought the Jews to תשובה more effectively than all 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses.

steps.title: The prophets added nothing to the תורה except reading the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses neither added to nor subtracted from the תורה, with one exception: they established מקרא מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses prophesied to Israel, and they did not take away or add anything to what is written in the תורה, except for the reading of the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: Picking up on the mention of '48 prophets and 7 prophetesses', the גמרא brings a ברייתא about them. This sets up the next discussion: how could the prophets add a new מצוה at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a נביא may not add new מצוות to the תורה. The ברייתא says the prophets kept to that rule with one exception, the reading of the מגילה. That exception raises an obvious question, which the גמרא is about to take up.
steps.whatToRemember: מקרא מגילה is the one מצוה the prophets added beyond what is written in the תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how unusual the מצוה of reading the מגילה is, and it leads straight into the גמרא's question of how the prophets were allowed to add it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Forty-eight prophets and seven prophetesses
prophesied to Israel,
and they did not subtract and did not add
to what is written in the Torah,
except for the reading of the Megillah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה נְבִיאִים וְשֶׁבַע נְבִיאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked to step 3 by the shared phrase '48 prophets and 7 prophetesses'; shifts from אגדה to a halachic point about מקרא מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prophets made no additions or subtractions to the תורה except instituting the reading of the מגילה.

steps.title: What reasoning allowed the prophets to add מקרא מגילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source or reasoning the נביאים used to add the מצוה of reading the מגילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the נביאים were allowed to add the מצוה of reading the מגילה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא just said the נביאים never added to or took away from the תורה. Adding מקרא מגילה looks like breaking that rule. So the גמרא wants to know what reasoning justified it.

keyTerms.meaning: What did they learn out? What was their reasoning?

phrases.english: What did they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the one addition named in the ברייתא of step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning the נביאים used to add מקרא מגילה.

steps.title: A קל וחומר: from death to life is greater than from slavery to freedom
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה explains that if we sing for leaving slavery, we surely must praise ה׳ for being saved from death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: If we say שירה for going from slavery to freedom, then for going from death to life, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the נביאים used a קל וחומר from יציאת מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At יציאת מצרים the Jews went from slavery to freedom, and we praise ה׳ for it. On פורים they went from a death sentence to life, which is an even bigger rescue. So praising ה׳ by reading the מגילה is required all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: If a smaller case gets a rule, a bigger case surely does

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that reading the מגילה is a form of praising ה׳, not only a history lesson. The next steps build on this idea.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Avin said
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
If for going from slavery to freedom
phrases.notes: This is יציאת מצרים.

phrases.english: we say song,
then for going from death to life, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the שירה said for יציאת מצרים.

steps.title: Then we should say הלל on פורים too
steps.stepSummary: If פורים is learned from יציאת מצרים, the גמרא asks why we do not also say הלל on פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we should also say הלל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the קל וחומר. If פורים is an even greater rescue, we should say הלל on it just as on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר should carry over everything from the smaller case. On פסח we say הלל, so on פורים we should say it too. Yet we do not, so the גמרא needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The chapters of תהלים said on holidays to praise ה׳

phrases.english: If so, let us also say Hallel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the קל וחומר in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קל וחומר from יציאת מצרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the קל וחומר works, it should require הלל on פורים too, but we do not say it.

steps.title: No הלל for a miracle outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: We do not say הלל on פורים because its miracle happened outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we do not say הלל on a miracle that happened outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פורים miracle took place in פרס, outside ארץ ישראל, and הלל is not said for such a miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a limit on הלל specifically. It does not cancel the קל וחומר for reading the מגילה. It only explains why הלל itself is left out.

phrases.english: Because we do not say Hallel
on a miracle that happened outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים הַלֵּל עַל נֵס שֶׁבַּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule of הלל by location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר requires הלל on פורים.
steps.terutzMaskana: הלל is not said for a miracle outside ארץ ישראל, so פורים has no הלל.

steps.title: But יציאת מצרים also happened outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the miracle of יציאת מצרים was in מצרים, so how do we sing about it?
steps.simpleTranslation: יציאת מצרים was also a miracle outside ארץ ישראל. How do we say שירה for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. It points out that the original case, יציאת מצרים, also happened outside the Land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a miracle outside the Land gets no praise, then יציאת מצרים should get none either. Yet we do praise ה׳ for it. So the rule from step 8 seems to contradict the source of the whole קל וחומר.

phrases.english: The Exodus from Egypt, which was a miracle outside the Land,
how do we say song for it?

steps.triggerLanguage: יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, דְּנֵס שֶׁבְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ, הֵיכִי אָמְרִינַן שִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that no הלל is said for a miracle outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יציאת מצרים was outside the Land, yet we praise ה׳ for it.

steps.title: Before entering the Land, every land was fit for שירה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that before the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, miracles in any land could get שירה. After they entered, only the Land qualifies.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Before the Jews entered the Land, all lands were fit for saying שירה. Once the Jews entered the Land, the other lands were no longer fit for saying שירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the challenge. Timing makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יציאת מצרים happened before the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, when all lands were equal, so it gets שירה. פורים happened after they had entered the Land, so a miracle in פרס does not get הלל. The answer from step 8 stands.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean פורים gets no praise at all. The מגילה reading is still required. The rule only removes הלל.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְתַנְיָא: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנְסוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָאָרֶץ —
phrases.english: As it is taught: Before the Jewish people entered the Land,
all lands were fit for saying song.
Once the Jewish people entered the Land,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ כׇּל הָאֲרָצוֹת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה.
phrases.english: all the other lands were no longer fit for saying song.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִכְנְסוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases by time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule about miracles outside the Land contradicts the שירה for יציאת מצרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Before the Jews entered the Land, all lands qualified. יציאת מצרים came before, פורים came after.

steps.title: רב נחמן: reading the מגילה is itself הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a different answer: we do not say separate הלל on פורים because reading the מגילה counts as הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Reading it is its הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a second answer to why there is no הלל on פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב נחמן, the place of the miracle is not the reason. פורים already has its praise, because the מגילה reading itself is the הלל. So nothing extra is needed.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קְרִיָּיתָהּ זוֹ הַלֵּילָהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Its reading is its Hallel.
phrases.notes: "Its" means the מגילה. Reading it is how we praise ה׳ on פורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: קְרִיָּיתָהּ זוֹ הַלֵּילָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the challenge of step 7 and gives a different answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Says the obligation is already fulfilled in another way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פורים should need a separate הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מגילה reading itself serves as הלל.

steps.title: רבא: we were still servants of אחשורוש
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the words of הלל do not fit פורים, because the Jews stayed under אחשורוש's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense there, with יציאת מצרים: 'Praise, servants of ה׳', and no longer servants of פרעה. But here, can we say 'Praise, servants of ה׳', and no longer servants of אחשורוש? We are still servants of אחשורוש!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a third answer: the words of הלל would not be true on פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל opens with 'הללו עבדי ה׳', meaning we serve only ה׳. After מצרים that was true, since the Jews were free of פרעה. After פורים the Jews were still in exile under אחשורוש, so the rescue was not complete and those words do not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Praise, servants of ה׳ (the opening of הלל)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three reasons there is no הלל on פורים. First, the miracle was outside ארץ ישראל after the Jews had entered the Land. Second, according to רב נחמן, the מגילה reading is the הלל. Third, according to רבא, we were still servants of אחשורוש.

phrases.english: Rava said: It makes sense there,
phrases.notes: "There" means יציאת מצרים.

phrases.english: "Praise, servants of God", and not servants of Pharaoh,
phrases.notes: The first פסוק of הלל, תהלים קיג.

phrases.english: but here, can we say "Praise, servants of God",
and not servants of Achashverosh?
We are still servants of Achashverosh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the challenge of step 7, alongside steps 8 and 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the words of הלל do not fit the situation after פורים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פורים should need הלל like פסח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rescue on פורים was incomplete, so 'הללו עבדי ה׳' does not fit and no הלל is said.

steps.title: Both new answers clash with the ברייתא about the Land
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, other lands were no longer fit for שירה. This is a problem for both רב נחמן and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both according to רבא and according to רב נחמן there is a difficulty: the ברייתא says that once the Jews entered the Land, the other lands were no longer fit for saying שירה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answers of רב נחמן and רבא. Both of them seem to ignore the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן and רבא gave other reasons for skipping הלל on פורים. That implies the פורים miracle would otherwise deserve הלל. But the ברייתא says miracles outside ארץ ישראל lost the right to שירה once the Jews entered the Land. So why look for other reasons, when the location alone should settle it?

keyTerms.meaning: Whether according to רבא or according to רב נחמן
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
song of praise to ה׳ for a miracle

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לְרָבָא בֵּין לְרַב נַחְמָן קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Both according to Rava and according to Rav Nachman, it is difficult:
But isn't it taught:
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא the גמרא quoted back in step 10.

phrases.english: Once they entered the Land,
all the other lands were no longer fit
for saying song!

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין לְרָבָא בֵּין לְרַב נַחְמָן קַשְׁיָא, וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answers of steps 11 and 12 using the ברייתא from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answers of רב נחמן (step 11) and רבא (step 12)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If lands outside ארץ ישראל are not fit for שירה, the פורים miracle never qualified for הלל. So the extra reasons of רב נחמן and רבא make no sense.

steps.title: After the exile, other lands became fit again
steps.stepSummary: Once the Jews were exiled, the other lands went back to their original fitness for שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they were exiled, the lands returned to their original fitness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב נחמן and רבא. The ברייתא's rule only applied while the Jews lived in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before entering the Land, miracles anywhere could get שירה. Once the Jews entered, only the Land counted. After the גלות, the Jews were no longer in the Land, so other lands became fit again. The פורים miracle happened during the גלות, so the location is not a problem. That is why רב נחמן and רבא needed other reasons.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule "only miracles in ארץ ישראל get שירה" applied only while the Jews lived in the Land. פורים happened in גלות, so the location alone does not cancel הלל. That is why רב נחמן (the מגילה is its הלל) and רבא ("we are still servants of אחשורוש") needed their own reasons.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this answer says we DO say הלל on פורים. It only explains why רב נחמן and רבא needed other reasons for skipping it.

phrases.english: Once they were exiled,
they returned to their original fitness.
phrases.notes: "They" means the other lands. They went back to how it was before the Jews entered ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the time frame of the ברייתא's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, other lands were unfit for שירה forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: The other lands were unfit only while the Jews lived in the Land. After the גלות they became fit again, so פורים needs a different reason.

steps.title: Weren't there two hundred prophets?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier count of 48 נביאים. The words "הרמתים צופים" are read as "one of 200 prophets."
steps.simpleTranslation: Were there really no more? But it is written: "And there was one man from הרמתים צופים," meaning one of two hundred prophets who prophesied for Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier teaching that there were 48 נביאים and 7 נביאות. It asks how that fits a פסוק that hints at 200 prophets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about אלקנה, father of שמואל הנביא, is read as a play on words. "רמתים" sounds like מאתים (200), and "צופים" means seers, which is another word for prophets. So אלקנה was "one of 200 prophets." That clashes with a total of only 48.

phrases.english: And there are no more?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the list earlier on the daf: 48 נביאים and 7 נביאות.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And there was one man
phrases.notes: This is the start of ספר שמואל (שמואל א׳ א:א), about אלקנה, שמואל's father.

phrases.english: from Ramathaim-zophim",
one of two hundred seers,
phrases.notes: A word play: "הרמתים" is read as "מאתים", two hundred.

phrases.english: who prophesied for Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הלל discussion and returns to the earlier count of נביאים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that there were 48 נביאים and 7 נביאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק, read through a word play, shows there were at least 200 prophets. That is far more than 48.

steps.title: Many prophets, but only the needed ones were written
steps.stepSummary: There really were very many prophets, double the number who left מצרים. Only prophecies needed for later generations were written down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, there were many, as it is taught: many prophets arose for Israel, double the number of those who left מצרים. But a prophecy that was needed for future generations was written down, and one that was not needed was not written down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both statements are true. There were huge numbers of prophets, but only 48 + 7 had their prophecies recorded in תנ״ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of 48 and 7 was never a count of every prophet who lived. It counts only the prophets whose messages were written down because they mattered for all generations. A ברייתא even says the true number was double the people who left מצרים, far more than 200.
steps.whatToRemember: The 48 נביאים and 7 נביאות are only the prophets whose messages were written down because later generations needed them. Many more prophets lived.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why תנ״ך includes some prophecies and not others: only messages with meaning for all generations were written down.

phrases.english: Indeed, there were many,
as it is taught:
Many prophets arose for Israel,
double the number of those who left Egypt.
But prophecy that was needed for future generations was written down,
and that which was not needed was not written down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 48 and 7 was a count of every prophet who ever lived.
steps.terutzMaskana: It counts only the prophets whose prophecies were written down for later generations. The total number was much higher.

steps.title: Two hills facing each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads "רמתים צופים" as a man from two hills that face each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: it means a man who comes from two heights that face one another.
steps.whatsHappening: A second explanation of "הרמתים צופים" is given. This one is about geography, not about prophets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "רמתים" means two heights, and "צופים" means looking out at. So the name describes a town on two hills that look at each other. In this reading, the words do not hint at 200 prophets at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
A man who comes from two heights
that face one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another way to read the פסוק quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "הרמתים צופים" means a place of two hills that face each other.

steps.title: Descended from people at the height of the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין reads "רמתים" as "רומו של עולם": אלקנה came from people who stood at the height of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said: it means a man who comes from people who stood at the height of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: A third reading of the same words is given. It is about אלקנה's family line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנין connects "רמתים" to "רום", height. He reads it as describing ancestors who stood at a very high place. Who those ancestors are is not yet said; the גמרא asks about it next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said:
A man who descends from people
who stand at the height of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same פסוק, alongside step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "רמתים" hints at ancestors who stood at the height of the world.

steps.title: Who are these people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the people standing at the height of the world were.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who are they?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short clarifying question that sets up the next step. The גמרא wants to know who רבי חנין means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנין's words are vague. The question asks which ancestors of אלקנה stood at the "height of the world."

phrases.english: And who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי חנין's phrase in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the people "at the height of the world"

steps.title: The sons of קרח on a high place in גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: They are the sons of קרח. They did not die, because a place was set aside for them in גיהנם and they stood on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of קרח, as it is written: "But the sons of קרח did not die." It was taught in the name of רבינו: a place was set aside for them in גיהנם, and they stood on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the people are the sons of קרח, from whom אלקנה came. It explains how they "stood at the height" of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the earth swallowed קרח, his sons were not killed, as the פסוק says. A ברייתא in the name of רבי adds that a special raised spot was made for them in גיהנם, and they stood on it. That raised spot is the "height of the world" in רבי חנין's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: our teacher, meaning רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of "הרמתים צופים": one of 200 prophets, two hills facing each other, or a man descended from the sons of קרח, who stood on a raised place in גיהנם.

phrases.english: The sons of Korach, as it is written:
"But the sons of Korach did not die" (Numbers 26:11),
It was taught in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: A place was set aside for them in Gehinnom,
and they stood on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי קֹרַח, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבְנֵי קֹרַח לֹא מֵתוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sons of קרח, who stood on a raised place set aside for them in גיהנם.

steps.title: Who were the seven prophetesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the names of the seven נביאות mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the seven prophetesses?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא said there were seven נביאות, and now the גמרא asks who they were. This question sets up the list that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps dealt with the 48 male prophets who were written down. Now the גמרא turns to the women prophets and asks for their names.

phrases.english: The seven prophetesses, who are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the male prophets and the sons of קרח to the women prophets listed in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The names of the seven prophetesses.

steps.title: The list of the seven prophetesses
steps.stepSummary: The seven are שרה, מרים, דבורה, חנה, אביגיל, חולדה, and אסתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: שרה, מרים, דבורה, חנה, אביגיל, חולדה, and אסתר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the seven women. Next it will bring a פסוק for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some names are surprising, like שרה, because the תורה never calls her a נביאה. That is why the גמרא now has to show a source for each woman.

keyTerms.meaning: Chulda, a prophetess in the days of King יאשיהו
Avigayil, who later became the wife of דוד

phrases.english: Sarah, Miriam, Devorah, Chana,
Avigayil, Chulda, and Esther.

steps.triggerLanguage: שרה מרים דבורה חנה אביגיל חולדה ואסתר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שרה, מרים, דבורה, חנה, אביגיל, חולדה, and אסתר.

steps.title: שרה is יסכה, who saw through רוח הקודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that 'יסכה' in the פסוק is שרה. She was called that because she 'saw' through רוח הקודש, as shown by 'listen to whatever שרה tells you'.
steps.simpleTranslation: שרה, as it is written: 'the father of מלכה and the father of יסכה.' רבי יצחק said: יסכה is שרה. Why was she called יסכה? Because she saw through רוח הקודש, as it says: 'Whatever שרה tells you, listen to her voice.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that שרה was a נביאה. It identifies her with 'יסכה' and explains that the name comes from seeing through רוח הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name יסכה is read as coming from a word for 'looking'. The proof that her seeing was real prophecy is that ה׳ told אברהם to listen to her.

keyTerms.meaning: Yiskah, a name in the פסוק; here it is שרה
Divine inspiration, a holy spirit of vision

phrases.english: Sarah, as it is written:
'The father of Milkah and the father of Yiskah,'
And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
'Yiskah' is Sarah,
And why was she called Yiskah?
Because she saw through divine inspiration,
phrases.notes: The name יסכה sounds like סכתה, meaning 'she looked'.

phrases.english: As it says:
'Whatever Sarah tells you,'
phrases.notes: ה׳ is speaking to אברהם here, telling him to send away ישמעאל as שרה asked.

phrases.english: 'listen to her voice.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שרה דכתיב אבי מלכה ואבי יסכה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first name on the list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The name יסכה in בראשית 11:29, read as 'seeing', backed up by 'כל אשר תאמר אליך שרה שמע בקולה'.

steps.title: A second meaning of יסכה: everyone gazed at her beauty
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation: she was called יסכה because everyone gazed at her beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'יסכה', because everyone gazed at her beauty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reason for the name יסכה, which is her beauty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both readings use the same root of 'looking'. In the first reading, she is the one who looks, through prophecy. In the second, others are the ones looking at her. The second reading adds praise but is not itself a proof of prophecy.

phrases.english: Another explanation: 'Yiskah',
because everyone gazed at her beauty.

steps.triggerLanguage: דבר אחר יסכה שהכל סוכין ביופיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name יסכה can also mean that all looked at שרה's beauty.

steps.title: מרים is called a נביאה outright
steps.stepSummary: מרים is explicitly called 'הנביאה' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרים, as it is written: 'And מרים the prophetess, the sister of אהרן, took...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that מרים was a נביאה because the פסוק calls her that directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no reading between the lines is needed, because the word 'הנביאה' is right there. But the wording 'the sister of אהרן' will raise a question in the next step.

phrases.english: Miriam, as it is written:
'And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took,'
phrases.notes: This is from the song at the sea, when she took a drum in her hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: מרים דכתיב ותקח מרים הנביאה אחות אהרן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second name on the list.

steps.title: Why only 'sister of אהרן' and not of משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why the פסוק calls her only אהרן's sister, when she was also משה's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not the sister of משה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a strange detail in the פסוק: it leaves out משה. This sets up רב's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was the greater and more famous brother, so you would expect him to be mentioned. Leaving him out must be hinting at something.

keyTerms.meaning: And not the sister of משה?

phrases.english: And not the sister of Moshe?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a difficulty with the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מרים was also משה's sister, so mentioning only אהרן seems incomplete and needs explaining.

steps.title: She prophesied before משה was born
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that she prophesied when she was still only אהרן's sister, before משה was born. When משה was born the house filled with light, and her father kissed her and said her prophecy came true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: She prophesied when she was only the sister of אהרן, and she said: 'My mother will have a son who will save ישראל.' When he was born, the whole house filled with light. Her father stood up, kissed her on the head, and said to her: 'My daughter, your prophecy has come true.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The פסוק says 'sister of אהרן' to hint at when she prophesied: before משה existed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אחות אהרן' describe the time of the prophecy, not just her family. When the house filled with light at משה's birth, it looked like clear proof her prophecy was true.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rav:
She was prophesying when she was only the sister of Aaron,
and she would say: My mother will give birth to a son
who will save Israel.
And at the time he was born,
the whole house filled with light,
her father stood up and kissed her on her head,
and said to her: My daughter, your prophecy has come true.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב נחמן אמר רב שהיתה מתנבאה כשהיא אחות אהרן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the פסוק mentions only אהרן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the phrase as marking the time of her prophecy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אחות אהרן' seemed to leave out משה for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase points to the time she prophesied, when she was only אהרן's sister, before משה was born.

steps.title: When משה was thrown in the river, her father doubted
steps.stepSummary: Once משה was put into the river, her father tapped her on the head and asked: 'My daughter, where is your prophecy now?'
steps.simpleTranslation: But once they threw him into the river, her father stood up, tapped her on her head, and said to her: 'My daughter, where is your prophecy?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב's story continues. When things looked bad for baby משה, her father questioned her prophecy. This sets up the פסוק the גמרא brings next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The kiss on the head turns into a tap on the head. The prophecy that seemed fulfilled now seemed in danger. This tension is what the next פסוק will describe.

phrases.english: But once they threw him into the river,
her father stood up and tapped her on her head,
and said to her: My daughter, where is your prophecy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב's story from the birth to the river.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When משה was thrown into the river, it seemed her prophecy might fail.

steps.title: His sister stood to see how her prophecy would end
steps.stepSummary: This explains the פסוק 'His sister stood far off to know': she wanted to know how her prophecy would end.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what is written: 'And his sister stood far away, to know.' To know what would happen with the end of her prophecy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the story to a פסוק. מרים stood by the river to see whether her prophecy would come true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain פסוק says she stood to know what would happen to משה. רב's story adds that what she was really waiting to see was the outcome of her own prophecy. So the story both explains the פסוק and is supported by it.

phrases.english: That is what is written:
'And his sister stood far away, to know.'
To know what would be with the end of her prophecy.

steps.triggerLanguage: היינו דכתיב ותתצב אחותו מרחוק לדעה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רב's story to a פסוק in שמות 2:4.
steps.raayaObject: רב's account that מרים prophesied about משה before his birth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 2:4, 'ותתצב אחותו מרחוק לדעה', read as waiting to see the end of her prophecy.
steps.whatToRemember: מרים is called 'sister of אהרן' because she prophesied about משה's birth before he was born. She stood by the river to see whether that prophecy would come true.

steps.title: דבורה is called a נביאה outright
steps.stepSummary: דבורה is explicitly called 'אשה נביאה' in ספר שופטים.
steps.simpleTranslation: דבורה, as it is written: 'And דבורה, a woman prophetess, the wife of לפידות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that דבורה was a נביאה because the פסוק says so directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like מרים, דבורה's prophecy is stated openly. But the strange phrase 'אשת לפידות' raises a question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of Lapidos; literally 'woman of torches'

phrases.english: Devorah, as it is written:
'And Devorah, a woman prophetess, the wife of Lapidos,'

steps.triggerLanguage: דבורה דכתיב ודבורה אשה נביאה אשת לפידות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third name on the list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 4:4, which explicitly calls her 'אשה נביאה'.

steps.title: What does 'אשת לפידות' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'אשת לפידות' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'אשת לפידות'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the unusual phrase in the פסוק. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לפידות' means torches or flames, which is an odd name. The גמרא wants to know what it is telling us about דבורה.

phrases.english: What is 'the wife of Lapidos'?
phrases.notes: Literally, 'a woman of torches', so the גמרא wants to know what the torches are about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the פסוק just quoted.

steps.title: She made wicks for the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: She was called 'אשת לפידות' because she made wicks for the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because she used to make wicks for the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'לפידות' (flames) refers to the wicks she made for the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of being the name of her husband, 'לפידות' is read as describing what she did. The wicks she made produced the flames of the מקדש's lights.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary; at that time, the משכן in שילה

phrases.english: Because she used to make wicks for the Mikdash.
phrases.notes: Wicks make flames, and לפידות means flames. That is the connection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אשת לפידות' means she made wicks, which produce flames, for the מקדש.

steps.title: Why does the verse mention the palm tree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that דבורה sat under a palm tree and asks why that detail matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And she sat under a palm tree.' What is special about sitting under a palm tree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still talking about דבורה and now asks why the פסוק bothers to say where she sat. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that every detail in a פסוק teaches something. Telling us she sat 'under a palm tree' seems unnecessary, so the גמרא looks for the lesson behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm tree (written תּוֹמֶר in this פסוק, the same word as תָּמָר)
What is different / what is special about this

phrases.english: "And she sat under a palm tree."
phrases.notes: This is from ספר שופטים, describing where דבורה sat when people came to her for judgment.

phrases.english: What is special about "under a palm tree"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining 'אשת לפידות', the גמרא explains another detail in the same passage about דבורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק tells us that דבורה sat specifically under a palm tree.

steps.title: She sat outdoors to avoid being alone with men
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אבשלום says the palm tree shows she judged in the open because of יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אבשלום said: It was because of the prohibition of a man and woman being secluded together.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: דבורה judged people under an open tree, not inside a house, so she would never be alone with a man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Men came to her for judgment. If she had judged indoors, she might have ended up secluded with one of them. Sitting outside in plain view solved that problem, so the palm tree detail teaches her care about יחוד.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and a woman being alone together in private, which is forbidden

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Avshalom said:
Because of seclusion.
phrases.notes: He means she judged out in the open so she would never be alone with a man who came to her case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אַבְשָׁלוֹם מִשּׁוּם יִחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The palm tree shows she judged in a public, open place to avoid יחוד.

steps.title: The palm tree as a symbol of one united heart
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: a palm tree has one heart, and so the Jews of that generation had one heart toward ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: just as a palm tree has only one heart, so the Jewish people in that generation had only one heart, directed to their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, symbolic answer. The palm tree stands for the people's undivided loyalty to ה׳ in דבורה's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A palm tree grows one main trunk without splitting into separate branches. The גמרא reads this as a picture of the generation: everyone was united and fully devoted to ה׳. This answer is about the people, while the first answer was about דבורה's own conduct.

phrases.english: Another explanation:

phrases.aramaic: מָה תָּמָר זֶה אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא לֵב אֶחָד —
phrases.english: Just as this palm tree has only one heart,
so too the Jewish people in that generation

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם אֶלָּא לֵב אֶחָד
phrases.english: had only one heart,
toward their Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר מָה תָּמָר זֶה אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא לֵב אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The palm tree symbolizes the generation's single-hearted devotion to ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the palm tree: (1) דבורה judged in the open to avoid יחוד; (2) it symbolizes the united heart of Israel in her time.

steps.title: חנה is a נביאה: the source verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to חנה and brings her prayer, 'רמה קרני בה׳', as the source showing she was a נביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנה was a prophetess, as it is written: 'And חנה prayed and said: My heart rejoices in ה׳, my horn is raised up in ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of נביאות and moves to חנה. It quotes her prayer, which will turn out to contain a prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא only gives the פסוק. The explanation of what makes it a prophecy comes in the next step, from the words 'רמה קרני'.

keyTerms.meaning: My horn (a symbol of strength and greatness)

phrases.english: Hannah, as it is written:
"And Hannah prayed and said:
My heart rejoices in ה׳,
my horn is raised up in ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes with דבורה and moves on to the next נביאה in the list, חנה.

steps.title: Horn, not jug: the prophecy about lasting kingship
steps.stepSummary: 'Horn' and not 'jug' predicts that kings anointed from a horn, דוד and שלמה, would have lasting kingship, while those anointed from a jug, שאול and יהוא, would not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'My horn is raised', and not 'my jug is raised.' דוד and שלמה, who were anointed from a horn, had kingship that continued. שאול and יהוא, who were anointed from a jug, did not have kingship that continued.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why חנה's words count as prophecy. By saying 'horn', she was predicting that horn-anointed kings would have lasting dynasties.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kings were anointed with oil from either a horn or a jug. History later showed that the horn-anointed kings, דוד and שלמה, kept their kingship in the family, while the jug-anointed kings, שאול and יהוא, did not. חנה hinted at this long before it happened, which proves she was a נביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their kingship continued (it lasted and passed on)

steps.whatToRemember: חנה's choice of the word 'horn' was a prophecy: kings anointed from a horn kept their kingship, and kings anointed from a jug did not.

phrases.english: "My horn is raised," and not "my jug is raised."
David and Solomon, who were anointed from a horn,
their kingship continued;
Saul and Jehu, who were anointed from a jug,
their kingship did not continue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the verse in step 36 shows prophecy.
steps.raayaObject: That חנה's words were real prophecy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The later history of the horn-anointed and jug-anointed kings matches her word choice.

steps.title: ה׳ outlasts what He makes
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר מנשיא reads 'בלתך' as 'לבלותך': unlike people, whose works outlast them, ה׳ outlasts His works.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'There is none holy like ה׳, for there is none besides You.' רב יהודה בר מנשיא said: Do not read it 'besides You' but 'to outlast You.' ה׳ is not like human beings. A person's handiwork outlasts him, but ה׳ outlasts His handiwork.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא is already discussing חנה's song, it explains another line of it. A small change in reading turns 'none besides You' into 'nothing outlasts You.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אל תקרי reading adds a second meaning to the פסוק without removing the plain one. When a person builds something, it usually lasts after he dies. ה׳ is the opposite: everything He creates eventually wears out, but He exists forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (only) this way, but (also) that way: a method that draws a second meaning from a פסוק
To outlast You (from the root בלה, to wear out)
Flesh and blood, a human being
The work of his hands, his creations

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not change the actual text of the פסוק or say the plain reading is wrong. It adds an extra layer of meaning.

phrases.english: "There is none holy like ה׳, for there is none besides You."
Rav Yehuda bar Menashya said:
Do not read "besides You," but "to outlast You."
phrases.notes: The letters are almost the same; reading them a little differently gives 'to wear out' or 'outlast'.

phrases.english: For not like the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood:
his handiwork outlasts him,
but the Holy One, Blessed be He,
outlasts His handiwork.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא אַל תִּקְרֵי בִּלְתֶּךָ אֶלָּא לְבַלּוֹתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side discussion: having quoted חנה's song, the גמרא explains its next line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ outlasts all His creations, unlike people, whose creations outlast them.

steps.title: No artist like our God
steps.stepSummary: 'צור' is read as 'צייר', an artist. People paint flat, lifeless forms, but ה׳ forms a baby inside its mother and gives it life and organs.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And there is no rock like our God': there is no artist like our God. A person draws a form on a wall but cannot give it breath, a soul, insides and intestines. But ה׳ forms a shape inside another shape and gives it breath, a soul, insides and intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains one more line of חנה's song by reading 'צור' (rock) as 'צייר' (artist). It then shows how ה׳ is a greater artist than any person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word צור sounds like the root for forming or drawing. A human artist makes only a flat picture with no life. ה׳ forms a child inside its mother, a form within a form, and gives it a living soul and working organs.

keyTerms.meaning: Rock (here also read as connected to forming)
A form inside a form: a baby inside its mother

steps.whatToRemember: חנה's song is read with three lessons about ה׳: her 'horn' was prophecy about kings, ה׳ outlasts His creations, and ה׳ is the ultimate artist who creates living beings.

phrases.english: "And there is no rock like our God":
there is no artist like our God.

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם צָר צוּרָה עַל גַּבֵּי הַכּוֹתֶל
phrases.english: A person draws a form on a wall

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַטִּיל בָּהּ רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה,
phrases.english: but cannot put breath and a soul into it,
insides and intestines.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא צָר צוּרָה בְּתוֹךְ צוּרָה,
phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He, forms a form inside a form,
phrases.notes: He means a baby being formed inside its mother.

phrases.english: and puts breath and a soul into it,
insides and intestines.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין צוּר כֵּאלֹהֵינוּ אֵין צַיָּיר כֵּאלֹהֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining חנה's song, moving to the next phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ is the supreme artist: He forms living beings inside their mothers and gives them a soul and organs.

steps.title: אביגיל is next on the list, with her verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק about אביגיל riding down 'בסתר ההר' as its starting point for showing she was a נביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביגיל was a prophetess, as it says: 'And as she rode on the donkey, she came down by the hidden side of the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: After finishing with חנה, the גמרא now turns to the next נביאה, אביגיל, and quotes a פסוק about her. This sets up the next move: the גמרא is about to point out something odd in the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse on its own does not openly say anything about prophecy. The גמרא brings it because one strange word in it, 'בסתר', will be unpacked to reveal a hidden story. That story is the start of the larger account of אביגיל's wisdom.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of נבל, who later married דוד. She is counted among the seven נביאות.
As it is written. This introduces a פסוק.
Literally 'in the hidden part of the mountain.' This is the key phrase of the step.

phrases.english: Abigail, as it is written:
"And it was, as she rode on the donkey,
phrases.notes: This is from שמואל א 25, when אביגיל rushes out to stop דוד from attacking her husband נבל.

phrases.english: and she came down by the hidden side of the mountain."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from חנה (steps 36-39) to the next נביאה on the list.
steps.raayaObject: That אביגיל was a נביאה (the full proof unfolds over the following steps).
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 25:20, 'וְהָיָה הִיא רוֹכֶבֶת עַל הַחֲמוֹר וְיוֹרֶדֶת בְּסֵתֶר הָהָר'.

steps.title: Why 'hidden side' and not just 'from the mountain'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק says 'בסתר ההר' when the natural wording would be 'מן ההר', from the mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it say 'by the hidden side of the mountain'? It should have said 'from the mountain'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the word 'בסתר' (hidden) seems out of place. If she came down a mountain, the פסוק should just say 'from the mountain.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra or unusual word tells the גמרא that the פסוק is hinting at something beyond simple geography. The question is about the wording, and it sets up a דרשה that will explain what 'hidden' refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: It should have said. The גמרא uses this to point out that a different wording would have been more natural.
From the mountain. This is the simpler wording the גמרא expected.

phrases.english: "By the hidden side of the mountain"?
It should have said "from the mountain"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'בסתר' in the פסוק about אביגיל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Describing a descent from a mountain should naturally say 'מן ההר'. The extra idea of 'hidden' seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Blood from hidden places: she showed דוד a blood stain
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל explains that 'סתר' hints at blood from the body's hidden places. אביגיל came to דוד with a blood stain and asked him to rule on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said: She came about the matter of blood that comes from the hidden places. She took blood and showed it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שמואל answers the question: 'בסתר' hints at 'סתרים', hidden places, meaning blood from a woman's body. אביגיל brought דוד a blood stain and asked him to rule on whether she was טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd word 'סתר' is now read as a hint to a halachic question about נדה blood. This turns a simple travel scene into a clever move. אביגיל opens a conversation about halacha with דוד, and this will let her slow him down before he harms נבל.

keyTerms.meaning: About the matter of. It introduces what she came about.
The hidden places. A modest way of referring to the private parts of the body. It links back to the word 'סתר' in the פסוק.
She took blood, meaning a blood-stained cloth.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel said:
About the matter of blood
that comes from the hidden places.
She took blood and showed it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: עַל עִסְקֵי דָם הַבָּא מִן הַסְּתָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the פסוק says 'בסתר'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word: 'סתר' is a hint to 'סתרים', blood from hidden places.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בסתר ההר' looked like an unnecessary description of a place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word hints that she came to דוד with a question about נדה blood.

steps.title: דוד: blood is not examined at night
steps.stepSummary: דוד answers her that one does not examine blood stains at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Do people show blood at night?
steps.whatsHappening: דוד replies to her question by refusing to rule. Blood stains are not examined at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling which colors of blood are טמא needs good light, so a ruling cannot be made by night. דוד is following the halacha carefully. That is exactly what אביגיל was hoping for, because now she can use his own carefulness.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it so that...? It opens a question that expects the answer 'no'.
Showing blood to a חכם so he can rule whether it is טמא.

phrases.english: He said to her:
Do people show blood at night?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: דוד responds to the blood she showed him.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether her blood stain makes her טמאה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No ruling is given, because blood is not examined at night.

steps.title: אביגיל: capital cases aren't judged at night either
steps.stepSummary: אביגיל turns דוד's rule back on him: just as blood isn't judged at night, capital cases aren't judged at night, so he cannot condemn נבל now. The step ends with 'אמר לה' as דוד begins to respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Are capital cases judged at night? He said to her:
steps.whatsHappening: אביגיל uses דוד's own carefulness against his plan. If he won't even rule on a blood stain at night, how can he sentence נבל to death at night? The amud ends with 'He said to her,' and דוד's answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the whole point of her clever question about the blood. She got דוד to show that he follows halachic rules about night. Then she pointed out that דיני נפשות, cases of life and death, are also not judged at night. That challenges his plan to kill נבל right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Judge, as in deciding a court case.
Capital cases, meaning cases where a person's life is at stake.

steps.whyThisMatters: This exchange shows the wisdom of אביגיל. She stopped דוד from spilling blood by reminding him of halacha instead of arguing with him head-on.

phrases.english: She said to him:
Are capital cases judged at night?
phrases.notes: She means: so you can't sentence נבל to death tonight either. דוד was on his way to kill him.

phrases.english: He said to her:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns דוד's own rule from step 43 into a challenge against his plan.
steps.kashyaTarget: דוד's plan to put נבל to death at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If halacha forbids ruling on blood at night, it certainly forbids judging capital cases at night. So נבל cannot be condemned now.
